context.requirement_text:
Second half of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix for its own stated PRIMARY
surface, atop REQ-216's core module. Mirrors REQ-186/REQ-187's and
REQ-214/REQ-215's own "core module first, wiring requirement(s)
second, disjoint files" split precedent in this file.

TWO ADMISSION GATES, NOT ONE, because tenant identity is not known
until partway through `Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline`'s existing chain --
read in full (lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex): `Plug.Parsers` runs
first, then `assign_trace_id`, then `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(which itself resolves tenant identity via a DB read -- token
verification, tenant-by-realm/slug resolution, JIT provisioning --
i.e. AuthPipeline's OWN work already consumes a DB connection BEFORE
any tenant identity exists to gate on), then
`Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`, then `match`/`dispatch`. Given that
ordering, a single per-tenant-only gate cannot run early enough to
cover AuthPipeline's own connection use. Resolved as follows, stated
as an accepted, disclosed limitation rather than silently glossed
over (matching this project's own honesty convention for a limitation
that cannot be fully closed within one requirement's scope, e.g.
decision 0014's own disclosed WASM native-crash gap):

1. GLOBAL gate, mounted FIRST in the chain -- before `Plug.Parsers`,
so a request rejected for lack of capacity is rejected before any
body-parsing work is spent on it. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)`. Covers AuthPipeline's own
connection use (the gap named above) because it runs before
AuthPipeline and gates ALL downstream DB-connection-holding work,
auth included.
2. PER-TENANT gate, mounted immediately AFTER `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(tenant identity now resolved into `conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id`)
and BEFORE `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`/`match`/`dispatch`. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire({:tenant, schema_name})`, resolving
`schema_name` the same way `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus` and
`Letflow.Scheduler.Poller` already do (tenant-id -> schema-name
resolution already exists in this codebase; reuse it, do not
re-derive). Covers TenantStatus's own DB lookup and every sub-router's
dispatch work -- the dominant share of connection-holding time per
REQ-056/ISS-0431's own round-trip profiling.
DISCLOSED LIMITATION: AuthPipeline's own DB work (steps 1-4 of its
moduledoc) is covered by the global gate only, not a per-tenant one,
because tenant identity does not exist yet at that point in the
chain. This is accepted, not silently omitted -- state it in this
plug's own moduledoc.
3. Both gates: on `{:error, :capacity}`, respond immediately (halt the
plug chain, no further plugs run) via
`Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2` (REQ-066, ALREADY
EXISTING -- do not add a new response helper), with the
`Retry-After` header set explicitly on the conn first (matching
`Response.rate_limited/2`'s own documented "caller sets Retry-After"
convention) to a fixed, configured seconds value (config, default 1)
-- NOT a computed estimate, since this admission mechanism has no
queueing/backoff-timing model to estimate from (a fixed short value
matching `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`'s own existing `@retry_after_seconds
"30"` precedent's SHAPE, though the specific number here is
independently justified: admission rejection is a near-instant
decision with no wait queue behind it, unlike TenantStatus's
migration-in-progress case, so a MUCH shorter retry-after is
appropriate -- state this reasoning in the plug's moduledoc rather
than copying TenantStatus's 30-second value uncritically).
4. On success at BOTH gates: the plug stores both `admission_ref()`s
in `conn.assigns` and registers a `Plug.Conn.register_before_send/2`
(or equivalent, matching how this codebase already threads
request-scoped cleanup -- state which mechanism is chosen and why) or
calls `Letflow.Admission.release/1` for both refs when the response is
sent, so an admitted request's slot is freed exactly once, on every
response path including a request that raises inside a downstream
plug or router (verified in the acceptance criteria below).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore logic;
no change to `Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit` (still deferred, unmounted,
unrelated mechanism); no Poller wiring (REQ-218); no tier-weighted
per-tenant caps (REQ-216's own recorded open question).

task.description: Implement the validated design doc §10 rework (lib/letflow/design/req217-http-admission-wiring.md lines 516-744, passed by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR at step-01f) on top of the already-implemented and already-committed REQ-217 code, fixing SECURITY-REVIEWER's step-03 double-global-consumption FAIL: add Letflow.Plugs.Admission.release_global_ref/1 to release the global gate's ref immediately after AuthPipeline completes, before the tenant gate's own try_acquire({:tenant, schema}) call, so a single request never holds two global units simultaneously.
acceptance_criteria: Letflow.Plugs.Admission.release_global_ref/1 exists, nil-checks conn.assigns[:global_admission_ref], calls Letflow.Admission.release/1 on it if present, removes it from the pdict list via List.delete/2, and sets conn.assigns[:global_admission_ref] to nil
a thin :release_global_admission plug wrapper (matching :assign_trace_id's pattern) is mounted in api_pipeline.ex between AuthPipeline and the pool: :tenant mount
test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs's AC3/AC4 global_cap minimum is re-derived from 2 to 1 and their comments updated to explain why
a test proves global_cap == 1 admits one full request end to end under the fix (and would not have under the old wiring)
mutation-testing verification: removing the new plug mount makes the global_cap == 1 test(s) fail; restoring it makes them pass again
mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force and mix test both pass with real quoted output

result.summary:
Implemented design doc §10.1 exactly.

1. lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex: added `release_global_ref/1` (public, @spec Plug.Conn.t() -> Plug.Conn.t()). Body: reads conn.assigns[:global_admission_ref] via a case; nil -> returns conn unchanged (defensive no-op, matches the design's stated posture); present -> (a) Admission.release(ref), (b) List.delete/2's the specific ref out of the @admission_refs_pdict_key list (Process.get/put, not a full clear), (c) assign(conn, :global_admission_ref, nil). Confirmed release_ref(nil) -> :ok already existed at line 184 exactly as CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's step-01f verdict said -- no gap found there, zero change needed to admit/3 or the existing before_send callback for Mechanism A to safely no-op on the now-nil assign. Also extended the moduledoc with a new paragraph documenting release_global_ref/1's mount point, purpose, and the accepted 'admission at the global gate is re-checked, not reserved' semantics per design doc §10.3's moduledoc obligation.

2. lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex: added `plug(:release_global_admission)` between `plug(Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline)` and `plug(Letflow.Plugs.Admission, pool: :tenant)`, plus the private 2-arity wrapper `defp release_global_admission(conn, _opts), do: Letflow.Plugs.Admission.release_global_ref(conn)` alongside the existing `assign_trace_id/2` wrapper -- same 'Plug.Router's plug DSL only accepts a local function atom, never a remote capture' pattern, matching the design's explicit instruction. Extended the moduledoc's admission-control section with the new plug's rationale and the re-checked-not-reserved semantics, mirroring what design doc §10.3 requires be stated in the shipped code.

3. test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs: updated the module moduledoc's chain description to include the new step; re-derived AC3's setup from `restart_admission!(pool_size: 3, reserved_headroom: 1)` (global_cap == 2) to `restart_admission!(pool_size: 2, reserved_headroom: 1)` (global_cap == 1, via the existing `max(pool_size - reserved_headroom, 1)` formula in test/support/admission_test_helpers.ex), rewriting the comment to explain the fix (global gate's ref is released before the tenant gate's own composing acquisition runs, so only one global unit is ever held at once). Did the same for AC4 (same pool_size/reserved_headroom change, comment updated to explain a leaked ref would now leave zero spare units instead of one). Extended AC6's chain-order test to also assert :release_global_admission's plug(...) source-text index falls strictly between AuthPipeline's and the tenant admission mount's.

4. NEW proof tests added (describe "REQ-217 rework (design doc §10.1): ..."): (a) 'global_cap == 1 admits one full request end to end' -- direct positive re-derivation of §10.4's flagged arithmetic, restart_admission!(pool_size: 1, reserved_headroom: 0), one real HTTP round trip through the real Router, asserts non-503/404. Under the OLD (pre-fix) wiring this same test setup would fail 503 (confirmed by the mutation test below), since a single request drew 2 global units under the old bug. (b) 'at no instant during a single request's lifetime are two global units held simultaneously' -- same global_cap == 1 setup, dispatches the request, then AFTER the response probes Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global) and confirms it succeeds and is immediately released, proving the counter returned to fully free (no leak) and, by virtue of global_cap == 1 having admitted the request in the first place, that no more than one global unit was ever held concurrently during its lifetime. PROOF KIND USED: I judged the strong indirect proof (global_cap == 1 sufficiency, both stated and directly re-run under mutation) more reliable and simpler to reason about than attempting to synchronize a `:sys.get_state`/pdict-length inspection to the exact mid-request instant between AuthPipeline completing and the tenant gate acquiring -- Letflow.Admission's synchronous GenServer.call/2-per-acquisition design gives no natural hook to pause a real request mid-flight without adding test-only instrumentation the design doc does not call for, and the task brief explicitly accepts this indirect proof as 'close to a full proof' since it is exactly the scenario the OLD code needed cap==2 for.

5. MUTATION-TESTING VERIFICATION (real, done for real): commented out `plug(:release_global_admission)` in api_pipeline.ex (reverting to the old double-consumption wiring), ran `mix test test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs` -- exactly 4 of 8 tests failed: AC3 ('cap of 1 concurrent request...'), AC4 ('a malformed :id...'), and both new proof tests ('global_cap == 1 admits...' and 'at no instant...'), all failing on `refute conn.status == 503` / `assert_raise` as expected -- every OTHER test (AC1, AC2, AC6, the chain-order assertion) still passed, confirming the mutation broke precisely and only the global_cap==1-dependent tests, not vacuously. Restored `plug(:release_global_admission)`, recompiled (`mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force` -- 'Compiling 184 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', zero warnings), reran -- 'Result: 20 passed', 0 failures. Reran the full test/letflow/plugs/ suite for regression -- 'Result: 113 passed', 0 failures.

COMMANDS RUN, IN ORDER, ALL FOREGROUND, REAL OUTPUT:
1. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force` -- 'Compiling 184 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app'. Zero warnings, zero errors.
2. `mix format` on lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex, lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex, test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs -- ran clean, `git diff --stat` unchanged by the format pass (already correctly formatted).
3. `mix test test/letflow/plugs/admission_test.exs test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs` -- 'Finished in 7.2 seconds' / 'Result: 20 passed', 0 failures.
4. `mix test test/letflow/plugs/` (regression) -- 'Finished in 21.0 seconds' / 'Result: 113 passed', 0 failures.
5. Mutation-test before/after -- see point 5 above: 4/8 failed with the plug removed (exactly the global_cap==1-dependent tests), 20/20 (targeted) and 113/113 (full plugs/) passed with it restored.

Self-review: did not touch process_instance.ex (no state-diagram update needed); no migration in this change; mix compile/format run and quoted above, not claimed without running. Both admission.ex and api_pipeline.ex moduledocs extended per design doc §10.3's explicit obligation to document the re-checked-not-reserved semantics in shipped code, not just the design doc.

Routing to SECURITY-REVIEWER for re-check, since this directly fixes the exact defect its own step-03 gate FAILED on. No change to Letflow.Admission's public API, state shape, or atomicity algorithm (confirmed: only lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex and lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex touched, per the design's own explicit constraint). No new tenant-data read/write introduced; release_global_ref/1 reads only conn.assigns[:global_admission_ref] (this process's own prior admission-ref, never tenant-suppliable) and the process-local pdict list.
